Q_001,How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?,"## Getting Food Assistance in California
You’ve lost your job and need help putting food on the table. Below is a simple guide to the main programs you can use right now.
### 1. **CalFresh (California’s SNAP program)**
The easiest way to get monthly food benefits is to apply for **CalFresh** – the state’s version of SNAP.

column3: A monthly benefit loaded onto an **EBT card** that you can use at grocery stores, farmers markets and some restaurants.

• You live in California.
• You are a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or qualified non‑citizen.
• Your household income is ≈ ≤ 200 % of the federal poverty level (exact % can vary by county).
• You have limited resources (cash, bank accounts, etc.).
Individuals ≥ 18 years old, families, seniors, people with disabilities, and households with children.

1. **Online:** Go to **[www.getcalfresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** or **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com)** and follow the step‑by‑step prompts.
2. **Phone:** Call the CalFresh Benefits Helpline **1‑877‑847‑3663** for help or to request a paper application.
3. **In‑person:** Visit your **County Social Services Agency** (often called the “Department of Social Services” or “Family Services”).

• Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).
• Proof of California residence (utility bill, lease, etc.).
• Social Security numbers for all household members.
• Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits notice, or other income proof.
• Bank statements (if you have a checking/savings account).

• **Initial interview** (phone or in‑person) – usually within 7 days.
• **Eligibility decision** – you’ll hear back within 30 days of completing the interview.
• If approved, you get an **EBT card** within 7‑10 days (often mailed).

• You can ask for **expedited benefits** if you have no food right now – they may start as soon as 3 days after the interview.
• Keep a copy of your application and any letters you receive.

Q_002,Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?,"## Yes – You can often receive **more than one** California assistance program at the same time

Most public‑benefit programs are **designed to stack** (work together). Getting help from one program usually does **not** stop you from applying for another, as long as you meet each program’s own rules.

column1: ### How the “stacking” works
1. **Each program looks at your own eligibility.**
- For example, CalFresh checks your household income and size.
- Medi‑Cal looks at income, immigration status, and medical need.
2. **Your **combined** benefits are still measured against each program’s limits.**
- Some cash‑aid programs (like General Assistance) have **time‑limit rules** (e.g., 3 months of aid per 12‑month period for people who are considered employable).
- Those limits do **not** affect food or health benefits.
3. **You may need to report when you start or stop another benefit.**
- When you get a new program, the agency may ask for a copy of the award letter or benefit statement.
- Keeping the agencies updated helps avoid over‑payments that you might have to repay.

column1: ### County‑by‑County Variations
- **Application portals** differ: some counties use **BenefitsCal.com**, others have their own online system.
- **Income limits** for cash‑aid programs (GA, CAPI) can vary slightly by county.
- **Local programs** (e.g., emergency rental assistance, utility assistance) may be offered in addition to state programs.
- **Office hours and contact numbers** are set by each county’s Social Services Department.

**What to do:** Call or visit your **county social services office** (or check the county’s website) to learn the exact steps and any extra local resources. A quick phone call can confirm whether you need to fill out a separate application for a county‑specific program.
### Other Programs That Might Help While You’re Unemployed
- **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** – if you lost a job through no fault of your own, you may qualify for weekly benefits.
- **Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) & Child Tax Credit (CTC)** – refundable tax credits that can give you a cash boost when you file your tax return.
- **Workforce Development / Job Corps** – county‑run job‑training and placement services (often free for low‑income adults).
- **Housing Assistance** – Section 8 vouchers, single‑room occupancy (SRO) subsidies, or emergency rent relief programs.
- **Energy Assistance (LIHEAP)** – helps pay heating/cooling bills; eligibility varies by income and utility provider.
- **Veterans Services** – if you’re a veteran, the VA offers cash assistance, health care, and job‑training programs.
- **Senior Services** – if you’re 65 or older, you may qualify for **Multipurpose Senior Services (MSSP)**, **Senior CalWORKs**, or **Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI)**.
### Quick Checklist for Applying to Multiple Benefits
1. **Make a list** of the programs you want to apply for.
2. **Collect all core documents** (ID, proof of residence, income proof).
3. **Apply to the most urgent program first** (usually health or cash aid).
4. **Keep copies** of every award letter you receive.
5. **When you apply to the next program, attach those award letters** as proof of qualifying household member.
6. **Follow up** with each agency within the expected timeline.
7. **Update any program when your situation changes** (new job, change in income, move, etc.).
### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job is stressful, but California has a network of **overlapping safety‑net programs** that can keep food on the table, health care in place, and utilities paid while you search for new work. Start with one application today, keep your paperwork organized, and reach out to your **county social services office** for personalized help.

column1: If you answer “yes” to the first two rows, you are **likely** eligible. The final step is to have a local WIC office verify your enrollment.
## What Is WIC?
- **W**omen, **I**nfants, and **C**hildren program
- Provides **nutritional education**, **breast‑feeding support**, and **benefits to buy healthy foods** (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, dairy, formula, etc.).
- Benefits are loaded onto a **California WIC Card** that works like an EBT card at approved grocery stores.
## How to Apply (Step‑by‑Step)
1. **Do the free online eligibility check**
- Visit the [WIC Eligibility Assessment](https://myfamily.wic.ca.gov/Home/HowCanIGetWIC) or call 1‑800‑852‑5770.
2. **Find a WIC office near you**
- Use the [Office & Grocer Locator](https://myfamily.wic.ca.gov/Home/WICOfficeGrocer) or search by city/ZIP on the site.
3. **Schedule an appointment**
- Most offices require an appointment (online or by phone). Some may accept walk‑ins, but calling first is safest.
4. **Gather required documents** (see the table below). Bring **all** for every family member you’re enrolling.
5. **Attend the first appointment**
- A counselor will review your documents, confirm eligibility, and complete a nutrition assessment.
- If approved, you’ll receive a WIC Card the same day.
6. **Start using your benefits**
- Shop at participating stores, use the WIC Card, and attend any nutrition or breastfeeding classes the office recommends.
## Documents You’ll Need

column1: ## 1. Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) – Basics

column3: Details
California residents who lost income (e.g., job loss, reduced hours) and are at risk of eviction or homelessness.
Up to **12 months** of past‑due rent, future rent, and (in many counties) utility arrears.

• Household income ≤ 120 % of the Area Median Income (AMI) – **most counties use this**.
• You must be a California resident and have a lease or rental agreement.
• Proof of rent owed (receipts, landlord notice, or cancelled checks).
Applications are reviewed in **2–6 weeks** after you submit all required documents. Processing time can vary by county.

• Rental/lease agreement or rent receipt.
• Copy of eviction notice or “pay‑or‑leave” notice.
• Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment benefits, bank statements).
• Photo ID (driver’s license or state ID).
• Utility bills (if you’re also applying for utility help).

column1: ## 2. CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Families) – Quick Overview
- **What it does:** Provides monthly cash aid that can be used for rent, utilities, food, medical care, and other essential needs.
- **Eligibility basics:**
- Must be a California resident with **low or no income** (usually ≤ 200 % of the Federal Poverty Level).
- Must have **children** or be pregnant, or meet other qualifying conditions (e.g., disability).
- **How to apply:** Call your **County Social Services Office** or apply online via the **BenefitsCal** portal.
- **Documents you’ll need:** Same as ERA, plus proof of citizenship/immigration status and any child‑care or medical expense paperwork.
## 3. Utility Help (LIHEAP & WAP)
If you also struggle with electric, gas, or water bills, the **Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)** and the **Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)** can provide:
- Up‑front cash to pay heating/cooling bills.
- Help with weatherizing your home to lower future costs.
**How to apply:** Call 211 or your local **Community Action Agency** (often listed on the LIHEAP state page).
## 4. What to Say When You Call

## 1. How to Get Started – Step‑by‑Step Checklist
1. **Gather Basic Information**
- Social Security Number (SSN)
- Driver’s license or state ID number
- Most recent employer’s name, address, and dates of employment
- Recent pay stubs or W‑2s (if you have them)
- Bank account info for direct deposit (EDD debit card)
2. **Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI)**
- Go to the **[EDD UI online application](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)** and follow the eight‑step process shown on the site.
- After you file, **register in CalJOBS** within 21 days (required to keep UI benefits).
3. **Create a CalJOBS Account**
- Upload a current résumé (or use the CalJOBS resume builder).
- Sign up for job‑search alerts and free workshops.
4. **Contact Your Local WorkForce Center**
- Find the nearest center via **[EDD Workforce Services Locator](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/)**.
- Make an appointment (online or by phone). Bring your ID, recent pay information, and UI claim number (if you have one).
5. **Explore Training Stipends (CTB) or TANF Vouchers**
- Ask the WorkForce counselor about the **California Training Benefits** (if you’re on UI).
- If you need cash assistance, ask about **TANF** and request a job‑training voucher.
6. **Apply for Additional Supports (if needed)**
- **Food:** Apply for **CalFresh** (SNAP) – quick online at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)**.
- **Health:** Apply for **Medi‑Cal** (California Medicaid) if you’re low‑income – start at **[Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/)** or your county social services office.
- **Energy Bills:** Check **LIHEAP** and **Weatherization Assistance Program** via your local **Department of Community Services & Development**.

## 3. County‑Specific Variations

- **Eligibility thresholds** (income limits, asset limits) for TANF, CalFresh, and other cash‑assistance programs are set **by the state** but **implemented by each county**; some counties may have additional local programs (e.g., emergency rental assistance, job‑fair events).
- **Appointment availability** at WorkForce Centers can differ; urban counties often have more open slots than rural ones.
- **Training providers** (community colleges, apprenticeship sponsors) may vary; a county’s Workforce Center can give you a list of approved providers nearby.

**Bottom line:** After you start the state‑wide process (UI, CalJOBS, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal), **call your County Social Services Agency** to learn about any extra help they offer. You can find contact info on the **[California Department of Social Services – County Directory](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Social-Services-Directory)** page.
## 4. Other Programs Worth Checking (Even If Not Directly Asked)
- **Paid Family Leave (PFL) & State Disability Insurance (SDI):** If you have a qualifying medical condition or need to care for a family member, you may get partial wage replacement.
- **Veterans’ Preference Hiring:** State agencies and many private employers give extra points to veterans.
- **AB 5‑Related Gig Worker Benefits:** If you were an independent contractor, you might qualify for **UI for gig workers** under the “mixed‑employment” rules.
- **Housing Assistance:** If you’re worried about rent, look into **Section 8**, **California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA) mortgage assistance**, or **local emergency rental assistance** programs.
- **Legal Aid:** If you face eviction, wage theft, or discrimination, free legal clinics are listed at **[Legal Aid at Work – California](https://legalaidatwork.org/)** and at county law libraries.

### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job can feel overwhelming, but California has a network of free services that can help you get back to work — and keep you supported while you do it. Start with the **UI claim** (it’s free to apply) and then connect with your **local WorkForce Center** for personalized job‑search help and training options. If you need food, health, or housing assistance while you look for work, the same agencies can guide you to those programs, too.
**Take the first step today:** file your UI claim online and set up a CalJOBS account. From there, a counselor can walk you through any additional benefits you may qualify for.

Q_006,How do I apply for Medi-Cal after a layoff?,"## Getting Started with Medi‑Cal after a Layoff

Losing a job can be stressful, but you can still keep health coverage. **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid program) is available to people whose household income falls at or below the federal poverty level (about 138 % FPL). A recent layoff usually drops your income enough to qualify.
### 1. Basic Eligibility Checklist

column3: What it means for you
You must live in California.
Household income (including any unemployment benefits) must be ≤ 138 % FPL. Your recent layoff will be counted; only the money you actually receive (e.g., final paycheck, UI) is considered.
U.S. citizens, permanent residents, refugees, asylees, and many lawfully present immigrants qualify. (See the **Immigration Status** link in the resources below.)
If you already receive a qualifying public‑assistance program (CalFresh, CalWORKs, SSI, etc.) you automatically qualify for Medi‑Cal.

column1: *Eligibility rules can vary a bit by county, so double‑check with your local office.*
### 2. How to Apply
You have three convenient ways to start the application:
1. **Online – BenefitsCal.com**
- Go to **[BenefitsCal.com – Medi‑Cal application](https://benefitscal.com/Help/program/medical/HCPDE?lang=en)**.
- Create an account, fill out the short survey, and upload the required documents.
- After you submit, the county will contact you (usually within 1‑2 weeks) for a brief eligibility interview.
2. **By Phone**
- Call the **Medi‑Cal Helpline**: **800‑541‑5555**.
- A representative can start your application over the phone and tell you where to mail or drop off any paperwork.
3. **In‑Person at Your County Social Services Office**
- Find the nearest office using the **[County Social Services Office Locator](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Social-Services-Offices)**.
- Bring a photo ID and proof of income (see document list below).
- Staff can help you fill out the application right there.
> **Tip:** If you already have a Covered California account, you can also apply for Medi‑Cal through Covered California’s portal.
### 3. Documents You’ll Need

column3: Examples (bring originals or clear copies)
Driver’s license, state ID, passport, or military ID.
Utility bill, lease/rent agreement, or mail addressed to you at a California address.

• Final paycheck stub(s)
• Unemployment Insurance (UI) award letter or benefit statement
• Letter from former employer confirming layoff (optional but helpful)
• Green card, visa, or other lawful‑presence document (see **[DHCS immigration docs guide](https://www.coveredca.com/documents-to-confirm-eligibility/immigration-status/)**).
CalFresh card, SSI award letter, CalWORKs notice, etc.

column1: If you cannot get a particular document right away, write a short letter explaining the situation, sign and date it, and attach it to your application.
### 4. What to Expect After You Apply

column3: Approx. Timeframe
1‑2 weeks.
Usually within 10 days of the review.
The state must decide **within 45 days** for non‑disability Medi‑Cal applications (often sooner).
If approved, retroactive coverage can begin as far back as the date you applied (often the first day of the month you filed).

Q_007,What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?,"## Unemployment Insurance (UI) – Income Limits
**California UI does not have a hard “income ceiling.”**

Instead, you must have earned enough wages during your **base period** (the first four of the last five completed quarters) to qualify. The amount you receive each week is **calculated from those past earnings**, not limited by a maximum household income.

column3: How it works
Your total wages from the first four of the last five completed quarters. You need a minimum amount of earnings (usually a few hundred dollars) to be eligible.
Determined by a formula that looks at your highest‑earning quarter in the base period. Weekly benefits range from **≈ $40 to $450** (2025 rates).
Set by the state each year; for 2025 it is about **$450**. You cannot receive more than this amount in a single week, regardless of how high your past earnings were.
Up to **26 weeks** (or longer if you qualify for extensions during a declared emergency).

column1: ### Bottom line
- **No income limit** that disqualifies you if you earn a lot now.
- You **must have earned wages** in the base period; if you have very low or no wages, you may not qualify.
- The **weekly amount is capped** at the state‑set maximum, not by your current income.

Unemployment Insurance (UI) gives a temporary weekly cash payment to workers in California who lost their job (or had hours cut) through no fault of their own.
### **Basic Eligibility**

## How to Apply
### 1. Gather Your Information
- ID, SSN, pay stubs, W‑2s, bank details, and a brief note of why you’re out of work.
### 2. Create a **myEDD** Account
- Go to the EDD website and click **“Apply Now.”**
- Follow the prompts to set up a username, password, and security questions.
- You’ll receive a **customer account number** by mail (usually within a week).
### 3. Submit the UI Claim (Step 2)

### 4. Register with **CalJOBS**
- After filing, you’ll be asked to create a CalJOBS account (the state’s job‑search portal).
- This is required for most UI claims; it also helps you find local job listings.
### 5. Review Benefit Documents
- The EDD will send a **Benefit Summary** (usually by email). It shows your weekly benefit amount and the date of your first payment.
### 6. **Certify** for Benefits Each Week
- Log in to **myEDD** or call **1‑800‑300‑5616** to certify you’re still unemployed and looking for work.
- You’ll need to report any earnings or job‑search activities for that week.
### 7. Receive Your First Payment
- Payments are usually made by **direct deposit** within **3 weeks** of your first successful certification.
- If you don’t have a bank account, you can request a **debit card** from the EDD.
### 8. Keep Up with Ongoing Requirements
- Respond promptly to any **Eligibility Questionnaire** (online, mail, or phone interview).
- Provide any extra documents the EDD requests (e.g., a separation notice or additional earnings proof).
- Failure to respond can delay or stop your benefits.

column1: ## How to apply for CalFresh (fastest way to get food help)
1. **Gather basic information**
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof of recent loss of income (termination letter, pay‑stub showing zero earnings, or a short written statement with the last work date)
- Proof of any other income you still receive (e.g., part‑time work, child support)
- Proof of address (utility bill, lease, or a letter from a landlord)
2. **Apply online** – Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com)** and select “CalFresh.”
- Fill out the short questionnaire; you’ll be asked for the documents above.
- After you submit, your county will call you within **1‑2 weeks** for a brief eligibility interview (often by phone or video).
3. **Complete the interview**
- Answer the questions honestly.
- If you have any trouble, the county worker can help you upload additional documents directly through the portal.
4. **Receive a decision**
- Most counties decide within **30 days**.
- If you qualify for **expedited service**, you’ll get a temporary EBT card in **3–5 business days** so you can start buying food right away.
5. **Keep your case active**
- Every month you’ll need to **recertify** (usually online) and report any changes in income or household size.
### Helpful links
- **Apply for CalFresh** – [BenefitsCal.com – CalFresh](https://benefitscal.com)
- **County contact list** – Find your local office’s phone number here: [California County Social Services Agencies](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks#main-content)
- **FAQ on how quickly you’ll get benefits** – [GetCalFresh FAQ](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq)
## How to apply for CalWORKs (if you have children)
1. **Check eligibility** – Must have at least one dependent child under 19 (or a disabled adult). Income and resources limits differ **by county**.
2. **Apply** – Same portal, **BenefitsCal.com**, choose “CalWORKs.” You can also call or visit your **County Social Services Agency**.
3. **Documents** – Same as for CalFresh, plus proof of the child’s identity (birth certificate, school ID).
4. **Timeline** – Decision also within **30 days**; emergency cash may be issued while you wait.
## Other programs you may want to explore right away

column1: ## What to do next (simple 3‑step plan)
1. **Apply for CalFresh today** on BenefitsCal.com – you’ll likely get an emergency card within a week.
2. **File an unemployment claim** with the EDD (you can do this at the same time).

3. **Contact your County Social Services Agency** – ask about CalWORKs, emergency cash, and any local food‑bank referrals. Keep a list of the documents you’ve already gathered; this will speed up each application.
### Remember
- **Every county may have slightly different rules and processing times**, so call the county office if you haven’t heard back after 2 weeks.
- **Provide any proof of income loss** you have (termination letter, email, or a short written statement) – it helps the caseworker understand your situation.
- **Do not wait** – the sooner you apply, the sooner you can get assistance.

Q_012,My company laid me off last month. I need help with EITC. What is this and how do I apply?,"## What is the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)?
The **Earned Income Tax Credit** is a tax “cash‑back” benefit for people who work and earn modest incomes.
* **Federal EITC** – paid by the IRS.
* **California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)** – paid by the state and adds extra money on top of the federal credit.
If you earned wages (or unemployment benefits) last year, you may be able to get money **even if you owe no tax**.
## Who can claim the credit?

## How to apply
1. **Gather your paperwork**
- **W‑2** from any employer (including your former employer)
- **1099‑G** if you received unemployment benefits (EDD)
- Social Security numbers for you, spouse/RDP, and any qualifying children
- Any proof that you stopped working (e.g., lay‑off notice) – helpful but not required
2. **Prepare your federal tax return**
- Use **Form 1040** (or 1040‑EZ/1040‑A if you qualify).
- Attach **Schedule 1** and **Schedule EIC** (the form that calculates the credit).
- Free help:
* **Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)** – available if you make $67,000 or less, have a disability, limited English, or are military.
* **Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE)** – if you’re 60 + .
3. **Prepare your California state return**
- Use **Form 540** (or 540‑2EZ) and include **Form 3514** to claim CalEITC.
- You can file online for free with **CalFile** (the FTB’s free e‑file system).
4. **File both returns** (federal first, then state).
- The **deadline** for the 2025 tax year is **April 15 2026** (or the next business day if the 15th falls on a weekend/holiday).
- If you miss the deadline, you can still file a **late return** and claim the credit; there is no penalty if you don’t owe tax.
5. **Check your refund**
- After the IRS processes your federal return, the state processes yours.
- Refunds are usually issued within 3‑4 weeks for e‑filed returns (longer for paper filings).
## What if I need to claim for a prior year?
You can amend up to **three years back** if you didn’t claim the credit before.
* File an **Amended Federal Return (Form 1040‑X)** and the matching state amendment (Form 540‑X).

column1: ## 1. Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI)
1. **Create a myEDD account** – go to the EDD website and click **Apply for UI**.
*Link*: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/step-2-apply/
2. **Enter your last employer’s information** and upload the lay‑off notice (UI‑101) if you have it.
3. **Certify every two weeks** (or weekly, depending on your claim) to keep receiving benefits.
*You have 21 days from the Notice of Requirement to Register for Work (DE 8405) and post your resume on CalJOBS.*
4. **Timeline** – EDD usually makes an initial decision within 2–3 weeks.  If you’re approved, you’ll receive the first payment by direct deposit or debit card.
## 2. Apply for CalWORKs (cash aid + child‑care)
1. **Find your County Social Services Agency** – look up “County Social Services Agency + [Your County]” or start at https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/cdss-programs/housing-programs.
2. **Complete the online application** on BenefitsCal.com (or you can get a paper form at the county office).
*Link*: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en (the same portal handles CalWORKs).
3. **Schedule the eligibility interview** (the county will call you within 1–2 weeks).
4. **If approved**, you can request **Child‑Care Assistance** for your toddler.  The county will help you pick a licensed provider and may cover most or all of the cost.
**Typical timeline** – Decision within 30 days of interview; child‑care assistance usually starts within a few weeks after you’re approved for cash aid.
## 3. Apply for CalFresh (food benefits)
1. **Apply online** on BenefitsCal.com (same portal as CalWORKs).
2. **Complete the eligibility interview** (often done by phone).
3. **If approved**, you’ll receive an EBT card loaded with monthly benefits.
**Timeline** – Up to 30 days for a decision; many counties process faster if you have all paperwork ready.
## 4. Apply for Medi‑Cal (health coverage)
1. **Apply online** at https://www.coveredca.com/medi‑cal/ or call your county’s Human Services Agency.
2. **Provide proof of income and residency** (same documents you used for CalWORKs).
**Timeline** – Coverage can begin the first day of the month after approval; most people get a decision in 2–4 weeks.
## 5. Apply for WIC (if you’re pregnant, breastfeeding, or have a child under 5)
1. **Call your local WIC office** or use the online eligibility tool: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DWICSN/Pages/HowCanIGetWIC.aspx.
2. **Bring proof of income** (benefit award letter, recent pay stub) and your child’s birth certificate.
**Timeline** – Usually a quick phone or in‑person appointment; you can start receiving vouchers within a few days of approval.
## 6. Get a Lifeline discount on phone or internet
1. **Check eligibility** – if you receive any of the above programs (CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, etc.) you automatically qualify.
2. **Apply** through a participating phone or internet provider’s website (search “Lifeline California”).
**Timeline** – Discount is usually applied within a few weeks of submitting proof of eligibility.

- Fill out the initial application (Step 1–2 on the EDD site).
- Answer the eligibility interview questions when an EDD representative calls (usually within a few days).
4. **Register in CalJOBS** *(Step 3 on the EDD site)*
- Create a free profile, upload a résumé, and start searching for jobs.
5. **Review Your Benefit Documents** *(Step 4)*
- You’ll receive a **Notice of Determination (DE 1080CZ)** showing your weekly benefit amount and the weeks you’re approved for.
6. **Certify for Benefits Weekly** *(Step 5)*
- Log in to UI Online each week, answer the certification questions, and **report any work or earnings** you had that week.
- **Certify promptly** – most counties require certification within 7 days of the week’s end.
7. **Receive Your First Payment** *(Step 6)*
- First payment typically arrives **about 3 weeks** after your claim is approved.
- Payments are loaded onto a **debit card** (Money Network) that EDD issues.
8. **Keep Certifying** *(Step 7)*
- Continue weekly certifications until benefits end or you find work.
9. **End Your Benefits** *(Step 8)*
- When you’re no longer eligible (e.g., you get a job), follow the “End Your Benefits” instructions to close the claim.

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

column1: ### How to Get Started – Step‑by‑Step
1. **Gather Your Documents**
- Photo ID for every adult (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Social Security numbers (or proof you’re applying for them)
- Proof of income (recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a statement that you have **no** income)
- Proof of California residence (lease, mortgage, or utility bill)
- Birth certificates for your newborn and toddler
2. **Call or Visit Your County Human Services Agency (CHSA)**
- Use **211** (dial 2‑1‑1) to get the phone number for your local office.
- Tell them you need help with **CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, and child‑care assistance**.
- Many counties can start a **combined application** for cash aid, food assistance, and health coverage.
3. **Apply Online (if you have internet access)**
- **CalWORKs / CalFresh / Medi‑Cal**: <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Applications>
- **Covered California**: <https://www.coveredca.com/>
- **WIC**: Find your local office and use the online eligibility assessment at <https://myfamily.wic.ca.gov/>
4. **Ask About County‑Specific Programs**
- **Child‑Care Subsidy** – each county runs its own program; the CHSA can tell you the application form and waiting list status.
- **Emergency Rental Assistance** – many counties have a “Housing Stabilization” or “Emergency Assistance” program with separate applications.
5. **Submit Your Application**
- Many programs allow you to upload documents online, but you can also bring printed copies to the CHSA.
- **Typical processing time:** 30‑45 days for cash aid and food benefits; child‑care and housing assistance may take longer, especially if there is a waitlist.
6. **Follow Up**
- After you submit, you’ll receive a **Notice of Determination** (mail or online) telling you what you qualify for and any next steps.
- If you need an appeal or have questions, the notice will include contact information.
### Quick Tips & Reminders
- **Don’t wait** – many benefits (especially cash aid, food, and health coverage) can start **within a few weeks** of a completed application.

- **You can get more than one benefit at the same time.** For example, a family can receive CalWORKs cash aid, CalFresh food benefits, Medi‑Cal health coverage, and WIC nutrition assistance simultaneously.
- **County differences matter.** Child‑care subsidies, emergency rent help, and some cash‑aid “supplemental” payments vary by county. Always confirm the local rules with your CHSA.

- **If you’re not a citizen**, you may still qualify for certain programs (e.g., **Cash Assistance for Immigrants (CAPI)**, **Medi‑Cal emergency coverage**, **WIC**). Bring your immigration documentation.
- **Ask about “interim assistance.”** If your cash‑aid application is still processing, many counties can give you a short‑term cash advance to cover urgent needs.
### Additional Resources
- **211 California** – dial **2‑1‑1** or visit <https://211ca.org/> for a directory of local help (housing, food banks, utility assistance).
- **California Department of Social Services (CDSS) – Programs Overview**: <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/>
- **Free Tax Help (VITA/TCE)**: <https://www.ftb.ca.gov/help/free-tax-help/index.html>
- **March of Dimes – Maternal & Infant Resources**: <https://osg.ca.gov/maternal-health-resources/>

**You’re taking the right first step by looking for help.** Gather your paperwork, reach out to your local County Human Services Agency (or call 2‑1‑1), and start the applications today. If any part of the process feels confusing, the staff at the CHSA are there to walk you through it, one step at a time.

column1: ## 2️⃣ Unemployment Insurance (UI) – State Benefits
**What it is** – Temporary cash assistance from the California Employment Development Department (EDD) for people who lost work **through no fault of their own**.
### Basic Eligibility
- You earned enough wages during the “base period” (usually the first 4 of the last 5 quarters).
- You are **able, available, and actively looking for work**.
- You are not refusing suitable work.
### How to Apply
1. **Create an online account** at the EDD portal: **[edd.ca.gov/ui](https://edd.ca.gov/ui/)**.
2. Fill out **UI Online Claim** (Form UI‑202).
3. Answer the weekly **Certification** questions each Friday.
### Documents You May Need
- Recent **pay stubs** or **W‑2s** from your most recent employer.
- **Driver’s license** or state ID number.
- **Bank account** info for direct deposit (optional but fastest).
### Timeline
- First payment typically **3–4 weeks** after you submit the initial claim.
- Weekly certifications keep the benefits flowing.
## 3️⃣ Emergency Rental & Utility Help
Many counties run **local Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) programs** funded by the federal COVID‑19 ERA and state resources. Rules can differ, so start with 211 or your county’s housing department.
### Common Eligibility Basics
- Household income at or below **80 % of the Area Median Income (AMI)** (exact limits vary by county).
- You’re at risk of eviction or already evicted.
- You must be a **California resident**.
### How to Get It
1. Call **211** or visit **[211.org/California](https://www.211.org/california)** to find the local ERA portal.
2. Complete the online or paper application (often a short questionnaire).
3. Provide:
- Proof of **income** (pay stub, unemployment benefits notice, or self‑employment documentation).
- **Lease agreement** or notice of eviction.
- Recent **utility bills** (if you’re applying for utility help).
### Timeline
- Most programs review applications within **2–4 weeks** and issue a **grant or loan** directly to the landlord or utility company.

- **You don’t need the old card** to get a replacement; just know your SSN.
- The SSA does **not charge** anything for a replacement.
- If you have a **temporary address** (e.g., staying with a friend), you can use it for the card, but you’ll need to update your permanent address later with other agencies.
## Updating Your Address After Moving
### 1. Social Security Administration (SSA)
- **Why?** Your SSA record is used when you apply for many California benefits (UI, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, etc.).
1. Log in to your **my Social Security** account online and edit the “Mailing Address.”
2. If you can’t log in, call **1‑800‑772‑1213** (TTY 1‑800‑325‑0778) and ask to update your address.
### 2. California Department of Human Services (for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, GA, etc.)
- Update through the **myBenefits** portal or call the program’s customer service line.
- **Note:** **Address‑change rules can vary by county** (some counties require a mailed form, others accept online updates). Check your **County Social Services** website for specifics.
### 3. California Employment Development Department (EDD) – Unemployment Benefits
- Log in to **EDD UI Online** and edit your contact information.
- You have **21 days** from the notice to register/update your work‑search record in **CalJOBS**; an outdated address can delay benefit payments.
## Will Changing Your SSN Card or Address Affect Benefit Applications?
- **Replacing the SSN card** **does not affect** any benefit eligibility. It’s just a new copy of the same number.
- **Updating your address** is important **so benefits reach you** (e.g., UI debit card, CalFresh benefits). If the address on file is wrong, payments may be delayed or sent to the wrong place.
- **Make the updates as soon as possible**—most agencies process changes within a few business days, but some counties may take longer.

Can I still get unemployment and also Medi-Cal?,"## Yes – You can often receive **both Unemployment Insurance (UI) and Medi‑Cal** at the same time, even if you have a severance payment and plan to do part‑time gig work. Below is a simple guide to help you understand how the programs work, what you’ll need, and the next steps to take.
## 1. How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works after a Severance

column4: What you should do

column3: Treated like a lump‑sum wage. It may **delay** your first UI payment until the severance “runs out.” The EDD will count the amount you receive each week and compare it to the weekly UI benefit amount.
column4:
• When you apply, **report the exact severance amount and the date you got it**.
• Keep any payoff statement or letter from your former employer.
• If you’re not sure how it will affect you, call the EDD at 1‑866‑401‑2849 or use the online chat.

column3: UI benefits are **reduced** by a portion of your earnings. In California you keep **$25** of your weekly UI benefit, then the rest is reduced by **½ of your earnings** (up to the full benefit).
column4:
• When you **certify each week** in UI Online, enter the exact amount you earned from the gig.
• You will still receive a reduced UI payment as long as you are “ready, willing, and able to work.”

column3: You can receive UI **and** Medi‑Cal at the same time. The UI amount you get is counted as income for Medi‑Cal, but many people still qualify because Medi‑Cal has very low (or no) cost for low‑income households.
column4: • Report both severance and gig earnings on your UI claim **and** on your Medi‑Cal application.

column3: Processing usually takes **about 3 weeks** after you submit the application. The first payment comes after the EDD has verified your eligibility and any severance impact.

3. **Fill out the application** – be ready to enter UI benefit amounts and any gig earnings.

If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

Losing a job is stressful, especially when rent and utility bills are coming due. Below is a quick guide to **emergency assistance you can apply for right now** while you file for Unemployment Insurance (UI).
## 1. Emergency Rental Assistance

## 2. Utility‑Bill Help
### Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
- **What it covers** – One‑time help with heating, cooling, or electric bills, plus emergency crisis assistance if your power is about to be shut off.
- **Eligibility** – Based on household income (generally at or below 150 % of the state median). Your exact limit varies by county.
- **How to apply** –
1. Find your county’s LIHEAP office: <https://www.csd.ca.gov/Pages/LIHEAPProgram.aspx> or call **211**.
2. You can apply **online**, **by phone**, or **in person** (some counties still require a paper form).
- **Documents needed** – Photo ID, proof of income, recent utility bill, and a copy of your lease or mortgage statement.
- **Timeline** – Many counties issue a decision **within 10‑14 days**; emergency crisis assistance can be faster (often within a few days).
### Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP)
- If you have a 24‑48‑hour disconnect notice, ask the utility for **ECIP** help. It’s part of LIHEAP but processed more quickly.
### Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
- Provides free home‑energy upgrades (insulation, weather‑stripping) that lower future bills.

- **How to start** – Contact your state WAP office: <https://www.usa.gov/help-with-energy-bills>. You’ll need proof of income and proof you receive another public benefit (e.g., UI, SNAP, or CalWORKs).
## 3. Unemployment Insurance (UI) – Quick Overview

3. **Gather documents** (list below) and keep them in one folder.
4. **Submit ERAP application** (or LIHEAP if rent assistance isn’t available).

## How to Avoid Overpayments
Overpayments happen when the agency pays more than you’re eligible for. Here’s how to keep them from happening:

column3: How to do it
Call or use the county’s online portal within **5 days** of a change in income, household size, address, or employment status.
Save pay stubs, unemployment award letters, and any side‑gig income.
If you’re unsure about a question, ask the caseworker to clarify.

column2: **Don’t accept extra money you’re not sure about**
column3: If you get a notice of “additional benefits,” verify it before spending the money.
Every month you’ll receive a notice showing the amount you’ll receive. Compare it to the amount actually paid.

column2: **Ask for a repayment plan if an overpayment occurs**
column3: If you do receive an overpayment, you can request a payment plan—don’t ignore the notice.

column1: If you ever get a notice of overpayment:
1. **Read the notice carefully** – it will explain why the overpayment was made.
2. **Call the agency** (the phone number is on the notice) within **30 days** to discuss it.
3. **Request a written repayment plan** if you can’t pay the full amount at once.
4. **Ask for a review** if you think the overpayment was a mistake. You have the right to appeal.

column1: ### How UI or severance impacts CalFresh
- **UI benefits are counted as income**. If your weekly UI amount is low enough, you’ll still qualify.

- **Severance pay is also counted as income**, but you only count it for the month you receive it. If the severance is a one‑time lump sum, it may temporarily push you over the limit for that month only. Tell the county worker the exact amount; they will calculate the effect.
- **Savings:** Most counties allow **up to $2,500** in countable resources (higher if someone is disabled or over 60). If your savings are below that amount, you’re fine.
### Timeline
- **Application submitted → interview (1‑2 weeks).**
- **Interview completed → benefits usually start within 30 days** of the interview.
- If you qualify for an **emergency food package**, you can get it **the same day** or within a few days of the interview.
## 2. Unemployment Insurance (UI)
### How to file
1. **Create a MyEDD account** at **[UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/FAQ_-_UI_Online/)**.
2. Follow the step‑by‑step wizard to **file your initial claim**.
3. **Schedule and attend the phone interview** (usually within 7‑10 days).
### Documents you’ll need
- Most recent **pay stub** or a **W‑2** from your last employer.
- **Severance agreement** (if you received severance).
- **Proof of identity** (same ID as for CalFresh).
### How severance can affect UI
- If you received **severance that is tied to a specific work period**, the EDD may treat that pay as wages for that period and **delay the start of UI** until the severance “runs out.”
- A **one‑time severance payment** that is not tied to a work period is usually **not counted** toward UI eligibility, but you must still report it on the claim.
### Timeline
- **Claim filed → phone interview (about 1 week).**
- **If approved, first payment** typically arrives **within 2‑3 weeks** of the interview.

column1: ### How the process usually works
1. **Apply** – online at the local county WIC site or submit a paper form.
2. **Schedule an appointment** – the county will contact you (often within a few days) to set a time.
3. **Attend the appointment** – a WIC counselor will verify your documents, do a brief nutrition assessment, and load any benefits onto a California WIC Card.
4. **Receive benefits** – you can start using the card immediately for eligible foods.

> **Note:** Every county runs its own WIC office, so the exact wait time for an appointment can differ. If you live in a large county (e.g., Los Angeles, San Diego) you may wait a bit longer than in a smaller county.

## 2. Will re‑applying for WIC affect your UI appeal?
**Short answer:** **No.**
- **Separate programs.**
* Unemployment Insurance (UI) is administered by the Employment Development Department (EDD).
* WIC is run by the county’s health department under the state’s Women, Infants and Children program.
- **Benefits do not “count against” each other.**
* Your UI eligibility is based on **your past wages** and how you meet the UI criteria (sources 5, 15).
* WIC eligibility looks at **current household income** and the presence of a pregnant person, infant, or child ≤ 5 years.
- **Appeal timeline stays the same.**
* You have **30 days** from the date of the Notice of Denial (DE 1080CZ) to file a written appeal (source 3).
* If you miss the 30‑day deadline, you can still ask for “good cause” to extend it (source 2).
- **What you should do:**
1. **Keep your UI appeal paperwork separate** and continue to certify for UI each week while the appeal is pending.
2. **Submit any UI‑required documents** (e.g., proof of earnings, ID) as soon as the EDD asks.
3. **Apply for WIC** whenever you’re ready; it will not interfere with the UI process.

[Source 13] I just lost my job - how does that affect my application for CalFresh?
URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

## Steps to get started
1. **Gather the paperwork** listed in the table (IDs, Social Security cards, recent pay stubs, lay‑off notice, rent/utility bill, birth certificates).
2. **Create an online BenefitsCal.com account** – this portal lets you apply for CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, and LIHEAP all at once.
3. **Fill out the application** for each program you want. You can submit one application and indicate you’d like to be considered for multiple benefits.
4. **Contact your county Social Services office** (you’ll find the phone number on the BenefitsCal site) to:
* Verify you’ve provided everything.
* Ask about any **county‑specific forms** (some counties require a local “Income and Resources” worksheet).
5. **Apply for any “quick‑start” programs** while you wait:
* **UI** (if you qualify) – file right away at EDD.ca.gov.
* **School meals** – talk to the school’s nutrition office.
* **Lifeline** – you can apply now using your Medi‑Cal or CalWORKs enrollment.

- **California Child Tax Credit (CCTC)** – a refundable credit for families with children; you claim it on your state tax return.

column1: ### What to Do First
1. **Gather basic documents** (you’ll need most of these for every application):
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof of immigration status (green card, work permit, DACA approval, refugee/asylee documents, etc.)
- Recent pay stubs or a letter showing you were laid off
- Recent bank statements showing low savings
- Social Security numbers for yourself and each child (if they have them)

2. **Call 211** (dial **2‑1‑1** or visit [211.org/CA](https://www.211.org/)). A trained specialist can point you to the exact county office numbers for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, ERAP, LIHEAP, and other emergency help.
3. **Apply online** where possible (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, Lifeline). Online portals often let you upload documents directly, which speeds up processing.
4. **Follow up by phone** if you don’t hear back within 30 days. Many counties have a “case manager” who can answer questions about status and next steps.
## Program Basics
### 1. CalFresh (Food Benefits)
- **What you get:** Monthly benefit card to buy groceries.
- **Eligibility:** Most legal non‑citizens (including DACA recipients, refugees, asylees, and those with a valid work permit) who meet income limits.
- **How to apply:** County office, phone, or the online **CalFresh portal**.
### 2. Medi‑Cal (Health Coverage)
- **What you get:** Doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, mental health services, and more.
- **Eligibility:** Similar immigration groups as CalFresh, plus some additional categories (pregnant people, children, seniors). Income limits are low‑to‑moderate.
- **How to apply:** County Human Services Agency, phone, or the **Covered California** enrollment site.
### 3. Emergency Rental & Utility Assistance
- **What you get:** One‑time help paying rent, mortgage, or utility bills.
- **Eligibility:** Income ≤ 80 % of area median income; many programs accept non‑citizens who meet the income test.
- **How to apply:** Call **211** or your local housing authority. Some counties have an online portal.
### 4. LIHEAP (Energy)
- **What you get:** Help with heating or cooling bills and sometimes weatherization.
- **Eligibility:** Low‑income households; non‑citizens can qualify if they meet the income test.
- **How to apply:** Contact your local **energy assistance agency** (often the same office that handles ERAP).
### 5. Lifeline (Phone/Internet)
- **What you get:** Discounted monthly payment for a landline, cell phone, or broadband internet.
- **Eligibility:** Income ≤ 135 % of the federal poverty level **or** participation in a qualifying program (e.g., CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, SSI).
- **How to apply:** Online at the **National Lifeline Support** site or through your service provider.
### 6. CalWORKs (Cash Assistance for Families)
- **What you get:** Monthly cash to meet basic needs while you look for work or training.
- **Eligibility:** Lawful residents and certain qualified non‑citizens; must have low cash on hand, meet income limits, and have dependent children.
- **How to apply:** County Human Services Agency (same office as CalFresh/Medi‑Cal).
### 7. General Assistance (County‑Specific)
- **What you get:** Cash for adults without dependent children who have little or no income.
- **Eligibility:** Varies by county; some counties accept certain non‑citizens.
- **How to apply:** Check your county’s social services website (e.g., Alameda County).
## What Happens to Your Information?

- **Sharing is limited to verification.** When you apply for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, or other state benefits, the county agency may check your data against other state programs (e.g., to see if you already get Medi‑Cal).

- **Federal privacy rules apply.** Your personal data is protected under the **Privacy Act** and the **California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)**. Agencies must keep information confidential and use it only for eligibility decisions.
- **No “selling” of data.** Agencies do **not** sell your information to private companies.
If you have concerns, ask the caseworker how your data will be stored and who will see it.

Q_032,"I live with my aunt and uncle, and just got laid off. My aunt has a disability. What should I do? I used to make about 45K. How much in benefits may I get if I apply for things? WHat  dates are important to remember? Any documnts?","## You’ve Been Laid Off – What to Do Next

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Below is a simple checklist of the main programs you can look into right now, the basic eligibility ideas, the paperwork you’ll need, and the key dates to keep in mind.
### 1. Unemployment Insurance (UI)

column3: **Temporary cash payments while you look for work**
Usually **$40‑$450 per week** – the exact amount depends on your past earnings (you earned about $45 K, so you’ll be toward the higher end).
Up to **26 weeks** in most cases; extensions may be available during a state‑wide emergency.

1. **Apply online** at the EDD portal (myEDD).
2. **Certify each week** you’re able and looking for work.
3. **Register on CalJOBS** (you have 21 days after you get the registration notice).

• **Apply within 4 weeks** of losing your job (you can still apply later, but you’ll lose weeks of benefits).
• First payment usually arrives **≈3 weeks after your application** if everything is complete.

• Driver’s license or ID card
• Social Security number
• Most recent pay stub(s) or W‑2 showing your $45 K earnings
• Employer’s name, address, and dates of employment
• Bank account info for direct deposit (or a debit card will be mailed).
[Unemployment Benefits – myEDD](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)

column1: ### 2. Food Assistance – **CalFresh (SNAP)**

column3: **Monthly benefit for buying groceries**

• You (or a household member) must have income at or below about **200 % of the federal poverty level** (exact numbers vary by county).
• Household includes anyone you live with who shares meals – **your aunt and uncle** are counted.

1. Go to **BenefitsCal.com** and start an online application.
2. Your county will call you within **1‑2 weeks** for an eligibility interview.

• Photo ID for each adult in the household
• Recent pay stubs or proof of last wages (your $45 K)
• Proof of any other benefits (e.g., your aunt’s disability payment)
• Rental or utility bill showing where you live
• Bank statements (if you have a checking account).
[Apply for CalFresh](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)

column1: ### 3. Health Coverage – **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid)

column3: **Free or low‑cost health insurance**

• Income ≤ **138 % of the federal poverty level** (or higher if you’re pregnant, disabled, or have other qualifying factors).
• Your aunt’s disability does **not** automatically qualify you, but you can apply based on your own income.

• Online at **Covered California** or call your county Human Services Agency.
• If you lose other coverage, you have up to **60 days** to enroll.

• ID, Social Security number
• Proof of income (most recent pay stub or tax return)
• Proof of residency (utility bill, lease)
[Covered California – Medi‑Cal enrollment](https://www.coveredca.com)

column1: ### 4. Lifeline Telephone/Internet Discount

column3: **Reduced phone or broadband bill**

• You, your aunt, or your uncle must be enrolled in **SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance, or a Veteran’s benefit**.
• You’ll need to show a benefit letter or official document for one of those programs.
Contact a Lifeline provider in California (many are listed on the Lifeline website) and submit proof of participation.

• Benefit letter (e.g., CalFresh award letter, Medicaid card)
• Photo ID
[Lifeline – Do I Qualify?](https://www.lifelinesupport.org/do-i-qualify/#income)

column1: ### 5. Emergency Rental & Utility Assistance

column3: **One‑time help paying rent, mortgage, or utilities**
• Income‑based, but many counties have **emergency funds** that don’t require strict means‑testing.

• Call **211** (dial 2‑1‑1) or visit the **California COVID‑19 Rental Assistance** site (still active for other emergencies).
• Your county social services office can point you to local programs.

• Proof of lease or mortgage statement
• Recent utility bill
• Proof of income (pay stub, unemployment award letter)
[Emergency Rent Assistance – USA.gov](https://www.usa.gov/emergency-pay-rent)

column1: ### 6. Cash Assistance for Families – **CalWORKs**

column3: **Cash aid for families with children or qualifying relatives**

• You must have a child in the home, or you’re caring for a foster child, or a relative (e.g., your aunt) who meets certain disability criteria.
• Income limits vary by county.
• Apply online at **BenefitsCal.com** or go to your **county social services office**.

• ID, SSN
• Proof of income (last pay stub)
• Proof of custody or care for the dependent (e.g., school records, foster documents)
[CalWORKs Overview](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks#main-content)

1. **Residency** – You must live in California (the program is county‑based).

2. **Income** – Generally at or below 150 % of the federal poverty level for LIHEAP/WAP, and at or below 300 % for CARE. Exact numbers change each year, so your county’s provider will confirm the current limit.
3. **Household size** – Include everyone who lives with you (you, your wife, your daughter).
4. **Utility bills** – You must have an active electric, gas, or oil account for the home you want help with.
5. **Other benefits** – If you already receive SNAP (CalFresh), Medicaid (Medi‑Cal), SSI, or TANF, you automatically meet the income test for most programs.
> **Note:** Income limits and application forms **vary by county**. Your local LIHEAP office will tell you the exact numbers for your area.
## 3. How to start the application process
1. **Gather needed documents**
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Recent pay stubs or a letter showing loss of employment (if any)
- Recent utility bill(s) showing account numbers and amounts owed
- Proof of residency (lease, mortgage statement, or utility bill with your address)
- Proof of any other benefits you receive (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, SSI, etc.)
2. **Contact your county’s LIHEAP office**
- Find the office here: <https://www.csd.ca.gov/energybills> → “Find Services in Your Area.”
- Call or visit the office (many offer same‑day appointments for emergency needs).
3. **Complete the application**
- Many counties allow an **online submission**; others require a paper form or an in‑person interview.
- Answer all questions fully – missing information can delay your case.
4. **Ask about “Fast Track” or emergency assistance**
- If you risk having gas or electricity shut off this winter, tell the staff right away. Some counties (e.g., San Bernardino’s CAP) have **Fast Track** services that speed up help.
5. **Follow up**
- After you submit, the office will review your case. Processing times differ, but most counties aim to **respond within 2‑4 weeks**; emergency requests can be approved in a few days.
- Keep a copy of everything you submit and note the case number.

If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. column3: Temporary cash benefit while you look for work.
